A USAF C-119 makes a mid-air recovery of the descending CIA Discoverer 14 spy satellite containing film from 17 passes over the Soviet Union. Near Hawaii. 1960

Discoverer 14 was a spy satellite launched by DARPA and the United States Air Force. On 19 August 1960, usable photographic film images of the Soviet Union taken by the satellite were recovered by a C-119 recovery aircraft. This was the first successful recovery of film from an orbiting satellite and the first mid-air recovery of an object returning from Earth orbit.

It was launched into a polar orbit by a Thor booster from Vandenberg AFB, California. After the Thor exhausted its fuel, the Agena A vehicle atop the Thor separated from it. Over Alaska on the 17th pass around the earth, the Agena ejected Discoverer 14 from its nose and, after it reentered the atmosphere, it released a parachute and floated earthward.

The descending satellite was sighted 360 miles southeast of Honolulu, Hawaii, by the crew of a US Air Force C-119 recovery aircraft. On its third pass over the parachute, the recovery gear trailing behind the aircraft successfully snagged the parachute canopy. A winch operator aboard the C-119 then reeled in the Discoverer after its 27-hour, 450,000 mile journey through space.
